exposure: 4-hour threshold for diagnosing active phase labor arrest
2-hour threshold for diagnosing active phase labor arrest
time threshold for diagnosing active phase labor arrest (2 hours vs. 4 hours)
cohort: Theoretical cohort of 1.4 million nulliparous U.S. women reaching 4 cm in spontaneous labor
finding: Increasing the time threshold for diagnosing active phase labor arrest from 2 to 4 hours was cost-effective, resulting in fewer cesarean deliveries and improved maternal outcomes, despite a small increase in adverse neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: A four-hour threshold leads to 56% more women having a vaginal delivery.
